1.why: Headings and body text use a clean sans-serif face with comfortable line height, although the small monospace text in the Logs panel is noticeably tighter.

2.why: Instructions such as 'Set up an extra check for protected payments.' are sentence-case with no italics or dense paragraphs, and the only all-caps text is the 'YOUR ONLINE BANK' brand label rather than an instruction.

3.why: The single-column card layout with full-width inputs and large buttons remains readable and would translate well to a phone-width screen.

4.why: Every prompt is a single short sentence, though terms like 'authenticator' and 'MFA' are unexplained technical language for a plain-language claim.

5.why: No field ever shows a placeholder, sample, or format hint; for example the 'Identity code' and 'Authenticator code' boxes are completely blank with no example of the expected six-digit input.

6.why: All the codes the user needs (identity value, provisioning secret, verification code) appear only inside the ever-growing monospace Logs panel, so the user must scan a dense text block to proceed.

7.why: The 32-character secret, one-time codes and recovery codes are rendered only as plain text with no copy button, download, or other copy affordance, so values must be transcribed by hand.

8.why: The authenticator setup screen offers only a 'Manual secret:' string; no QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is presented at any step.

9.why: There is no password field and the code boxes are plain text inputs with no visible one-time-code autofill support, so at best only the email and mobile fields could benefit from browser autofill.

10.why: Each screen pairs a bold step heading ('Verify your identity', 'Save recovery codes') with one prominent blue button, and an orange focus ring highlights the active control.

11.why: Each step asks for a single primary action; the only extra controls are the leftover 'Create secure setup code' / 'Generate recovery codes' buttons, which serve as secondary re-request options rather than competing main actions.

12.why: Screens generally just swap to the next form without stating what happened (e.g., after verifying identity), and plain status feedback lives only in the technical Logs panel until the final 'Multi-factor authentication is active.' message.

13.why: The error banner invites the user to 'Please try again' and codes can be re-requested via the same buttons without penalty, but no reveal/hide toggles exist for any code.

14.why: The single observed error, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is blame-free but never identifies the actual problem or the specific fix.

15.why: No countdown, expiry notice, or session timeout appears on any screen, so reading is untimed and code entry shows no visible time limit.
